===== crispcloud-wordperfect-UPSTREAM.md =====
Source: crispcloud-wordperfect-UPSTREAM.md (engines/wordperfect/UPSTREAM.md)
# Selected WordPerfect engine

This directory contains explicit source overlays for the Apache-2.0 WordPerfect
wrapper in [File Viewer at d264009ca6efb3daed79a39d1ae63133e0f25558](https://github.com/flyfish-dev/file-viewer/tree/d264009ca6efb3daed79a39d1ae63133e0f25558/packages/renderers/wordperfect).
`UPSTREAM.json` records the original source, runtime, fixture and notice bytes;
the entries marked as test material are only for validation. The runtime closure
uses libwpd 0.10.3 and librevenge 0.0.6 under the **MPL-2.0 election**, the MIT
callback shim, Boost under BSL-1.0, and the permissive native toolchain grants
listed in the upstream notice book. The root Apache license is not substituted
for those component licenses.

## Build and host contract

Copy the pinned `packages/renderers/wordperfect` package to staging and overlay
this directory's `src/*.ts` at its `src/` paths. Bundle `src/entry.ts` as the
browser renderer and `src/wordperfect.worker.ts` as a separate module worker.
The entry exports `renderWordPerfect(buffer, target, context)` and a default
alias. Context uses the existing File Viewer type-only contract; no core
runtime, npm parser, external service or approximate text fallback is imported.

The renderer needs the following same-origin runtime siblings, normally under
the host's flat `assets/runtime/` directory:

| Asset | Source |
| --- | --- |
| `wordperfect.worker.js` | Bundled selected `src/wordperfect.worker.ts` |
| `libwpd.mjs` | Unchanged upstream `vendor/libwpd.mjs` |
| `libwpd.wasm` | Unchanged upstream `vendor/libwpd.wasm` |

Context can provide local `wordPerfect.workerUrl` and `wordPerfect.wasmUrl`;
the loader is resolved beside the worker. The host must serve them using its
HTTP(S) origin, permit module workers and WebAssembly, and abort the context
when a file is closed or replaced. Both `destroy()` and `unmount()` dispose the
rendered instance. Native platforms use the host's local browser surface; this
slice does not add a native libwpd FFI build or claim native platform validation.

## Intentional modifications

- Require the actual structured libwpd engine. A missing worker, unsupported or
  corrupt file, encryption, timeout, or WASM failure rejects the preview.
- Preserve paragraph/table callback order, including tables in running
  sections. Keep a partially open body paragraph and its styles/links across a
  note. Header, footer and note content remain separately displayed.
- Display a persistent fidelity notice: page layout, embedded images/fonts,
  equations and drawings are not reproduced; table cells use plain text.
- Reject source above 64 MiB before copying, importing or allocating in WASM.
  Limit the decoded wire to 32 MiB, 200,000 events, 1,000 metadata pairs,
  8 MiB aggregate string bytes, 20,000 rendered blocks, 50,000 table cells,
  1,000-row/column spans and 16 nested document sections. Reject malformed or
  unfinished structures instead of rendering a misleading partial document.
- Keep parsing in a module worker with a maximum 60-second deadline. Abort,
  message/transfer errors and parser failures terminate that worker. Runtime
  URLs must use the local viewer origin. Links are rendered as text-safe DOM
  content; the shared host controls any external navigation.

These are input, output and time bounds. The unchanged native parser can
allocate internal working memory before it returns; these checks do not claim
to replace its compiled WASM memory ceiling or prove arbitrary-file safety.

## Distribution and source obligations

Preserve this Apache license and modification notices. Stage upstream
`THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`, all `vendor/libwpd-src/LICENSE*` documents,
`NATIVE_PROVENANCE.json`, `PROVENANCE.md`, `shim.cpp`, the three checksum-pinned
source archives, and `scripts/build-libwpd-wasm.mjs` as the corresponding source
and notice materials. The MPL-covered libraries and MIT shim are unchanged.
Their exact source is retained, including the fixed Xberg source URLs documented
by upstream. An application distributor must keep the MPL source availability
and notice requirements when distributing the runtime. The source and license
materials must remain reachable from the delivered app/source distribution;
this README alone is not a replacement for them.

The native runtime is copied after hash verification, **not rebuilt** by this
integration. WPD loader SHA-256 is
`ccd3267ce9cac2961bb6a500761753efa05c93563e7a5e46a31594cceb5e3096`;
WASM SHA-256 is
`bbfe0c7f712a357e3f9d11f9cf96d931e7cf4b9165d4379af78bf1bcb69333f0`.
No fonts, sample documents or complete File Viewer bundles are runtime assets.

## Focused validation

After installing the pinned dependencies in `../../tooling`, run from the app
root, supplying the exact upstream checkout if it is not a sibling directory:

```sh
FILE_VIEWER_UPSTREAM_DIR=/path/to/file-viewer node --test packages/file_viewer_documents/engines/wordperfect/test/wordperfect.test.mjs
```

The suite stages original files plus overlays into a temporary directory and
uses the package's esbuild. It checks malformed streams, ordering/sections,
limits, allocation-before-validation regressions, local assets and worker
lifecycle. It also runs the exact WASM against hash-verified, redistributable
WP 4.2, 5.0, 5.1 and 6.x fixtures. Fixture licenses and provenance remain in the
pinned upstream test directory; fixtures are not added to the app runtime.

`test/browser-smoke.mjs` separately checks both engine renderers in Chromium,
including visible warning text, ordered DOM tables, CHM sandbox/topic links,
sanitization and disposal. It requires a Playwright browser installation or an
explicit `CHROME_EXECUTABLE`. Local execution was blocked before browser startup
by the workspace socket policy; this is not recorded as a browser pass.


===== crispcloud-chm-UPSTREAM.md =====
Source: crispcloud-chm-UPSTREAM.md (engines/chm/UPSTREAM.md)
# Selected CHM engine

This directory contains source overlays for the Apache-2.0 CHM wrapper in
[File Viewer at d264009ca6efb3daed79a39d1ae63133e0f25558](https://github.com/flyfish-dev/file-viewer/tree/d264009ca6efb3daed79a39d1ae63133e0f25558/packages/renderers/chm).
`UPSTREAM.json` records original source, runtime, fixture and notice bytes.
The real Rust ITSF/LZX parser includes MIT adaptations from RustChm/FastChm;
its lockfile and complete packaged license book identify the Apache, MIT, BSD
and Unicode grants for Rust/WASM dependencies. This route does not use chmlib,
libmspack or a remote conversion service.

## Build and host contract

Copy the pinned `packages/renderers/chm` package to staging, then overlay this
directory's `src/*.ts` onto its `src/` paths. Bundle `src/entry.ts` as the browser
renderer and `src/chm.worker.ts` as a separate module worker. The entry exports
`renderChm(buffer, target, context)` and a default alias. Core imports in this
selected path are type-only; no full File Viewer core bundle is necessary.

The host's flat local runtime directory must include:

| Asset | Source |
| --- | --- |
| `chm.worker.js` | Bundled upstream worker with selected model overlay |
| `chm_wasm.js` | Unchanged upstream `src/wasm/chm_wasm.js` |
| `chm_wasm_bg.wasm` | Unchanged upstream `src/wasm/chm_wasm_bg.wasm` |

The context may override local `chm.workerUrl`, `chm.wasmModuleUrl` and
`chm.wasmUrl`. All must use the viewer's HTTP(S) origin. The host must support
module workers, WebAssembly, blob/data archive resources and a nested topic
iframe. Keep that topic iframe sandbox at `allow-same-origin` **without
`allow-scripts`**. The upstream HTML/CSS/SVG sanitizers and topic CSP remove
active content and block remote requests. Abort the context and destroy the
rendered instance on file replacement or close.

## Intentional modifications

- Enforce a hard 64 MiB input maximum before DOM construction or worker transfer.
  Bound the selected route to 20,000 archive entries, 16 MiB per decoded entry,
  128 MiB declared/unique decoded content, 4 MiB HTML/metadata, 2,000 search
  topics and 200 results. Lower host-supplied limits are preserved. Every worker
  request has a maximum 60-second deadline.
- Preserve and display parser warnings and references to additional merged
  archives. Only the selected archive is opened; related CHM files are not
  fetched automatically or represented as available topics.
- Restrict worker/loader/WASM URLs to the local origin. Abort closes the archive
  worker; failed transfers, initialization and malformed inputs reject cleanly.
  A failed initial render is propagated to the host instead of reporting ready.
- Retain the real archive table of contents, keyword index, search, local topics,
  resource resolution, sanitizers and object-URL cleanup.
- Resolve topic link targets using DOM capabilities rather than a parent-realm
  `instanceof Element` check, so links inside the topic iframe can navigate to
  another internal topic.
- Display sanitized topic HTML through one same-origin blob URL instead of
  `srcdoc`, matching the native host's restricted child-frame navigation policy.
  Revoke the previous topic URL on navigation and the final URL on disposal.
  The topic still has no script permission and retains its restrictive CSP.

Input/output limits are not claims that arbitrary native parsing is infallible.
The unchanged Rust/WASM runtime retains its own allocation, metadata, depth,
directory and decompression bounds. Initial topic readiness and cross-platform
host behavior need the shared browser/native host checks in addition to parser
tests.

## Distribution materials

Preserve the Apache license and modification notices, upstream
`THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`, `rust/LICENSE`, `rust/NOTICE.md`,
`rust/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md`, `rust/Cargo.toml`, `rust/Cargo.lock`,
`rust/rust-toolchain.toml`, the full `rust/src/` source and the upstream build
scripts. The source test fixture is used only by tests and is not a runtime
asset. Native parser sources and committed native outputs are unchanged.

The JavaScript loader SHA-256 is
`e7f1a6e0de035e7178c04a0307f52806997c9971a948e333e66a49fbe73a3d5c`;
WASM SHA-256 is
`02904a83ae8be928d5c90b9fd61faf28d8ba7e67ee96e3aeeb5d5b5102691538`.
This integration copies those hash-verified artifacts; it does not claim to
have rebuilt the native binary or to approve unrelated File Viewer bundles.

## Focused validation

After installing pinned `../../tooling` dependencies, run from the app root:

```sh
FILE_VIEWER_UPSTREAM_DIR=/path/to/file-viewer node --test packages/file_viewer_documents/engines/chm/test/chm.test.mjs
```

The suite stages exact source plus overlays in a temporary directory and uses
the shared test helper under `../wordperfect/test/`. It verifies limits, warning
retention, path/CSS/SVG protections, local runtime URLs, transfer and cancellation
lifecycle, then runs the pinned WASM against the real LZX-compressed fixture to
check contents, index, search metadata, HTML and local CSS resources. Malformed
archives and native parser limits must reject, with no text fallback.

The separate `../wordperfect/test/browser-smoke.mjs` covers both engines in a
real Chromium browser. Local execution was attempted but blocked before browser
startup by the workspace socket policy; a successful CI/browser run is still
required for end-to-end DOM and iframe navigation evidence.

# Selected spreadsheet source and modification notice

Source: [flyfish-dev/file-viewer](https://github.com/flyfish-dev/file-viewer/tree/d264009ca6efb3daed79a39d1ae63133e0f25558/packages/renderers/spreadsheet), immutable commit **d264009ca6efb3daed79a39d1ae63133e0f25558**, package `@file-viewer/renderer-spreadsheet` **3.3.3**. Original renderer source is **Apache-2.0**, Copyright 2026 Flyfish Viewer. This selected route also imports the Apache-2.0 File Viewer core. `UPSTREAM.json` records exact original source, original license/notice, and test-material identities; test material is not an app runtime asset.

The original source checkout remains unchanged. During the root build, these `src/` overlays replace the corresponding files under `packages/renderers/spreadsheet/src`. `entry.ts`, `limits.ts`, `zipPreflight.ts` and `boundedWorker.ts` are new integration files. `spreadsheet.ts` and `spreadsheet/worker/sheetjs/parser.ts` are modified copies. Their leading modification notices and the corresponding Apache grants must be retained.

## Modifications and execution boundary

The selected entry retains the original styled grid, worksheet tabs, supported styles, formula display and supported embedded images. Shared OOXML chart-rendering code also remains, but does not establish chart support for the newly routed XLS/XLT/XLSB formats: BIFF inputs skip chart extraction, and the ZIP chart extractor requires `xl/workbook.xml` rather than XLSB's `xl/workbook.bin`. It requires a local module worker, removes the upstream main-thread fallback, waits for the first displayed grid window, and propagates initial failures. Cancellation, worker errors and a 30-second deadline release resources. `unmount()` releases owned DOM and the active worker.

Added limits cover source bytes, actual streamed ZIP inflation, aggregate expanded data, worksheet count/dimensions/cell text, merges/drawings/metadata and row-window requests. A row-limited parse that reports a larger original range is rejected, not presented as a complete workbook. Defaults are detailed in [README.md](README.md) and the original integration source. File input is 32 MiB; ZIP expansion is 64 MiB total/32 MiB per entry; display ceilings are 128 sheets, 100,000 rows, 512 columns and one million populated cells. There is no text substitute on failure and no added macro execution.

Bundle the staged `entry.ts` as the entry and staged `spreadsheet/worker/sheetjs/sheet.worker.ts` as **`sheet.worker.js`** in the same flat runtime directory. The fixed URL resolves from `import.meta.url`; caller-supplied worker URL/mode options do not override it. Native browser hosts must enforce their separate networking, navigation and lifecycle rules.

## Distribution licenses

Retain the original renderer `LICENSE` and `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`, the core/root Apache-2.0 grant, and the actual npm package license/notice payloads selected by the root build. The selected direct closure includes styled-exceljs 0.21.6 (Apache-2.0), e-virt-table 1.4.17 (MIT), JSZip 3.10.2 (MIT election), pako 1.0.11 (MIT/Zlib), xmldom 0.9.12 (MIT), tinycolor2 1.6.0 (MIT), UTIF 3.1.0 (MIT), plus their realized bundled transitive dependencies. The root lockfile and `RUNTIME_MANIFEST.json` identify exact versions and every notice's source/hash; `assets/licenses/THIRD_PARTY.txt` retains all complete grants with exact originals in source-only `notices/`. Those component grants are not replaced by the root Apache license.

The selected source has no full File Viewer preset, unrelated renderer, embedded sample document, external conversion service or font asset. Browser/layout fidelity is separate from parser success. Node tests and browser bundle checks passed locally; an actual browser pass requires the CI smoke script, as local Chromium startup was blocked by the workspace socket policy.

# Selected PostScript and EPS preview

The selected File Viewer adapter and worker are Apache-2.0 at
[`d264009ca6efb3daed79a39d1ae63133e0f25558`](https://github.com/flyfish-dev/file-viewer/tree/d264009ca6efb3daed79a39d1ae63133e0f25558/packages/renderers/design).
Only its PostScript path is selected. Photoshop/Illustrator/Introspect and other
engines from the design package are not imported by this entry.

## Native artifact, sources and grants

The unchanged native engine is **Stet 0.8.7 / stet-wasm 0.2.0**, from
[`AndyCappDev/stet@58c7066817f7939789c6f030515c02e94fb0353b`](https://github.com/AndyCappDev/stet/tree/58c7066817f7939789c6f030515c02e94fb0353b).
Stet offers Apache-2.0 OR MIT; this selection elects Apache-2.0 and retains both
complete original texts. It is not a Ghostscript/libgs engine.

The 14,706,940-byte WASM has SHA-256
`b8d72531ec41ca497d67a79589a1dbb44748a4fefd088aa122007fbb28e06b20`.
The worker verifies that hash before compilation. The generated JavaScript
binding, WASM, embedded fonts/profile and native source are unmodified.
The original locked native provenance, toolchain versions, asset hashes and
source links are retained in `provenance/`; `UPSTREAM.json` ties those originals
to this selection. No independent native rebuild is claimed.

Retain the full `licenses/` directory:

- Stet Apache-2.0/MIT code licenses.
- **URW Base35 font assets under OFL-1.1**, including their reserved-name and
  modification conditions. These are separately licensed assets embedded in
  the WASM, not Apache fonts and not the user's opened fonts.
- **CGATS001Compat-v2-micro ICC profile under CC0-1.0**, with the original
  profile notice and complete CC0 legal text. Its source bytes are not the
  similarly named Ghostscript profile.
- The upstream native license book contains 91 conservative locked source
  packages and full original Rust/crate license materials. It includes
  host/build alternatives and is not a post-link claim that all listed
  packages are present. The underlying grant families are permissive (including
  MIT, Apache, BSD, Zlib and retained data/toolchain notices).

## Host and build contract

Stage upstream `packages/renderers/design/src`, then overlay this directory's
`src`. Bundle `entry.ts` and `postscript.worker.ts` as separate ES modules in the
flat runtime directory; copy unchanged `runtime/postscript/stet_wasm_bg.wasm`
there. The entry exports a default `(buffer, target, context)` renderer. The
worker bundles the original `src/postscriptRuntime/stet_wasm.js` binding.

Runtime URLs are fixed to that same HTTP(S) origin. The host needs module
workers, WebAssembly, `crypto.subtle`, Canvas 2D and an abort signal on close or
source replacement. The options under `context.options.design` may lower the
hard limits; they cannot raise them or replace the worker/native asset URL.
The worker deadline minimum is one second and the PS VM limit minimum is 16 MiB.

## Local modifications, 2026-11-13

- Cap the input at 32 MiB, published output at 200 pages, source dimensions at
  100,000 units, individual canvases at 8,192 pixels per side and 16 million
  pixels, and the interpreter's PostScript VM at 128 MiB. Every worker request
  has a terminating deadline of at most 30 seconds. These are specific input,
  interpreter and output limits, not a whole-browser RSS guarantee.
- Preserve lower host-supplied limits. The LRU cache targets 32 MiB while keeping
  the current raster; one 64 MiB RGBA page may therefore exceed that cache
  target. Print preparation checks a 128 MiB combined decoded working set.
- Fetch the native binary with a 16 MiB streamed asset cap, no redirects,
  omitted credentials, same-origin enforcement and the reviewed SHA-256.
  Other worker network APIs are disabled. Native PS cannot request additional
  files from the host through this adapter.
- Validate returned raster dimensions and RGBA length before transfer to the
  viewer. Return native failure/limit errors rather than text or metadata as a
  purported rendered result.
- Correct the page-cap boundary: Stet needs an additional EOF step after its
  final `showpage`. Accept a document exactly at the cap, rejecting immediately
  after the first extra completed page. At most one extra native page can
  complete before rejection, still inside the PS VM and worker-time bounds;
  no partial over-limit preview is returned.
- Clean up the worker, raster/print caches, observer, zoom provider, listeners
  and DOM both on normal destruction and on initial rendering failure or abort.
  Retain upstream latest-request-wins page rendering and bounded print logic.

The output is real CPU rasterization with Stet's embedded fonts and color
profile. The engine remains experimental and is not claimed to implement every
Adobe PostScript Level 3 extension or match reference print output.

## Validation

```sh
FILE_VIEWER_UPSTREAM_DIR=/path/to/file-viewer node --test packages/file_viewer_documents/engines/postscript/test/postscript.test.mjs
FILE_VIEWER_UPSTREAM_DIR=/path/to/file-viewer node packages/file_viewer_documents/engines/postscript/test/browser-smoke.mjs
```

The Node suite runs the genuine pinned WASM and production worker/client through
an explicit Node worker-thread transport fixture. Only local asset transport
and the Worker event interface are adapted; the interpreter/compiler is not
replaced. It checks real PS/EPS raster pixels, the exact page-cap boundary,
malformed inputs, native artifact verification, cancellation and timeout.
It does not qualify browser Worker/CSP/Canvas integration.

The separate Playwright script exercises those browser boundaries and the
rendered canvas/page controls on an enabled CI runner. Local Chromium could not
start because process socket creation was denied, so no local browser pass is
claimed. Install the pinned tooling and Chromium, or set
`CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE`. Authored PS/EPS test fixtures are Apache-2.0 and are not
runtime assets.

The CMYK ICC profile this crate embeds (resources/default_cmyk.icc) is
CGATS001Compat-v2-micro.icc from Clinton Ingram's Compact ICC Profiles
collection, byte-identical to
https://github.com/saucecontrol/Compact-ICC-Profiles/blob/1fabe4a41b/profiles/CGATS001Compat-v2-micro.icc
(8464 bytes, SHA-256
73e1ba37d2bad5bab2a964f40a9eed96209666efc067c3322626214bbef234a0).
Its own copyright tag reads "CC0".

It is not covered by this crate's Apache-2.0 OR MIT licence. That
collection's README releases it to the public domain:

    All profiles in this collection are released to the public domain
    under the Creative Commons CC0 license. They are free from
    restrictions on distribution and use to the extent allowed by law.

The CC0 1.0 Universal legal code is at
https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/legalcode

The file keeps the name default_cmyk.icc because it stands where
Ghostscript's profile of that name once stood. It is not that profile and
contains nothing from it: Ghostscript's default_cmyk.icc is 187484 bytes,
describes itself as "Artifex CMYK SWOP Profile", and carries an Artifex
copyright. The profile here is built from the CGATS TR 001-1995 (SWOP)
characterisation data.

===== crispcloud-xml-UPSTREAM.md =====
Source: crispcloud-xml-UPSTREAM.md (engines/xml/UPSTREAM.md)
# Selected XML validation and transformation tools

The selected Apache File Viewer sources are pinned to
[`d264009ca6efb3daed79a39d1ae63133e0f25558`](https://github.com/flyfish-dev/file-viewer/tree/d264009ca6efb3daed79a39d1ae63133e0f25558/packages/renderers/text).
`UPSTREAM.json` records original source hashes, published runtime versions and
copied grant files. This adapter does not include the complete text renderer.

## Runtime and grants

- `xmllint-wasm` **5.3.0**, MIT wrapper and libxml2 MIT-style grant, performs
  real XSD validation in a disposable module worker. `xmllint-browser.mjs` and
  `xmllint.wasm` are unchanged published assets.
- `xslt-polyfill` **1.0.33**, BSD-3-Clause wrapper, supplies the embedded
  libxml2/libxslt/libexslt MIT-style engine in `xslt-wasm.js`. The published
  asset is unchanged. Before compilation, the inherited Apache memory guard
  caps its defined WASM memory at 1,024 pages (64 MiB), without changing
  instructions or data.
- The libxml2 revisions are `c34742f3017f6d39f3e4ccae4f70172238160ef8`
  for XSLT and `eb0a2f2b91566384f378d870ffcd69c0a24162cc` for XSD;
  libxslt/libexslt uses `923903c59d668af42e3144bc623c9190a0f65988`.
  The published xmllint build links zlib, whose exact version is not identified
  by its npm metadata. The retained upstream notice states that limitation and
  includes the Zlib grant conservatively. No independent native rebuild is
  claimed.
- DOMPurify **3.4.17** offers `MPL-2.0 OR Apache-2.0`; this route selects
  Apache-2.0. Its complete original license is retained. The existing selected
  File Viewer core decoding helper is Apache-2.0.

Preserve `LICENSE`, `licenses/`, this modification notice and the exact
published package inventories from the shared build manifest. Font packages,
remote schemas, full text-formatting runtimes and unrelated File Viewer
renderers are not required by this selection.

## Host and build contract

Stage upstream `packages/renderers/text/src`, then overlay this directory's
`src`. Bundle `entry.ts`; it exports `renderXml` and a default alias with
`(buffer, target, context)`. Keep these files in the same flat runtime directory:

| File | Source |
| --- | --- |
| `xmllint-browser.mjs` | xmllint-wasm 5.3.0 published package |
| `xmllint.wasm` | xmllint-wasm 5.3.0 published package |
| `xslt-wasm.js` | xslt-polyfill 1.0.33 `dist/xslt-wasm.js` |

The host supplies a same-origin HTTP(S) document surface with blob workers,
WebAssembly and sandboxed blob frames. Its `context.signal` must be aborted on
replacement/close. Optional `context.options.xml.limits` can lower the input,
resource and output limits; `timeoutMs` may lower the per-operation deadline
from 15 seconds to at least 100 ms. Higher host values never raise hard caps.

## Local modifications, 2026-11-13

- New local-file/paste UI for independent XSD validation and XSLT 1.0
  transformation. The input source is never rewritten. XML and text
  transformation results are shown as exact output source. HTML also gets an
  inert preview; it is not reported as a faithful executable web page.
- Hard limits: 4 MiB original/decoded UTF-8 XML, 2 MiB schema/stylesheet,
  4 MiB output, 2 MiB per selected runtime asset, 15 seconds per operation,
  64 MiB XML WASM memory. Runtime fetches are same-origin, streamed/bounded
  and reject redirects.
- Keep the upstream DTD/entity, XInclude, schema dependency, XSLT
  import/include, `document()` and extension-instruction rejection. The
  actual worker disables network APIs and XSD also uses `--nonet`.
- Extend the worker result with its engine-reported media type and support
  standard `html`, `xml` and `text` output. Verify result pointers before
  decoding bounded output. Only HTML creates a preview iframe.
- HTML output is sanitized and sandboxed without script permissions. It has
  a `default-src 'none'` CSP; links, forms, refresh/base elements and external
  navigation attributes are removed. File inputs and other form controls are
  also removed because a sandbox alone does not prevent user-activated native
  file pickers. Only the trusted XML tools retain schema/stylesheet selectors.
  The exact original transformation output remains available as text.
- Cancellation destroys disposable workers. New resources invalidate older
  results; local file reads cannot replace a later selection. Destroy aborts
  work, clears data, removes listeners and revokes preview object URLs.

## Validation

Deterministic Node tests run with:

```sh
FILE_VIEWER_UPSTREAM_DIR=/path/to/file-viewer node --test packages/file_viewer_documents/engines/xml/test/xml.test.mjs
```

They exercise resource guards and byte/memory limits, genuine xmllint XSD
validation and genuine embedded libxslt transformations. XML DOM guard unit
checks use the real xmldom parser under Node. Those checks are not browser DOM,
worker or CSP qualification.

Real browser acceptance is separately runnable on an enabled Linux CI runner:

```sh
FILE_VIEWER_UPSTREAM_DIR=/path/to/file-viewer node packages/file_viewer_documents/engines/xml/test/browser-smoke.mjs
```

Install the pinned tooling dependencies and Playwright Chromium first (or set
`CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE` to an available compatible Chromium). Browser cases cover
valid/invalid XSD, real HTML/XML/text transformation, external-resource
rejection, user-click schema/stylesheet file chooser events, output bounds,
cancellation, cleanup and inert HTML without form controls. Browser chooser
events exercise the selected File API inputs; platform-native chooser dialogs
are qualified separately by their host tests. Local Chromium
was unavailable because process socket creation was denied; browser success is
not claimed until the real CI script completes. No fake compiler or replacement
WASM is used by either set of engine tests.

===== crispcloud-xml-licenses-NOTICE.md =====
Source: crispcloud-xml-licenses-NOTICE.md (engines/xml/licenses/NOTICE.md)
Source: xml-NOTICE.md (packages/renderers/text/licenses/xml-profiles/NOTICE.md)
# Optional XML profile runtimes

Retain this directory when redistributing the runtime assets. File Viewer's own
adapter is Apache-2.0; upstream engines retain their original licenses.
The asset helper copies engine files unchanged. During XSLT execution the adapter
limits the WASM memory declaration to 64 MiB before compilation; it does not change
the engine's instructions or data, nor install the automatic page polyfill.

| Component | Verified upstream notice | Included notice |
| --- | --- | --- |
| xslt-polyfill 1.0.33 | [BSD-3-Clause](https://github.com/mfreed7/xslt_polyfill/blob/4c0603c4dc84c17a511816c703c7ce3b936aa56f/LICENSE) | xslt-polyfill-LICENSE.txt |
| xmllint-wasm 5.3.0 | [MIT](https://github.com/noppa/xmllint-wasm/blob/master/COPYING) | xmllint-wasm-COPYING.txt |
| XSLT libxml2 submodule | [Copyright at c34742f](https://github.com/GNOME/libxml2/blob/c34742f3017f6d39f3e4ccae4f70172238160ef8/Copyright) | libxml2-xslt-Copyright.txt |
| XSD libxml2 submodule | [Copyright at eb0a2f2](https://github.com/GNOME/libxml2/blob/eb0a2f2b91566384f378d870ffcd69c0a24162cc/Copyright) | libxml2-xsd-Copyright.txt |
| libxslt and libexslt | [Copyright at 923903c](https://github.com/GNOME/libxslt/blob/923903c59d668af42e3144bc623c9190a0f65988/Copyright) | libxslt-Copyright.txt |
| zlib | [Upstream notice](https://github.com/madler/zlib/blob/develop/LICENSE) | zlib-LICENSE.txt |

The xmllint [build command](https://github.com/noppa/xmllint-wasm/blob/master/script/compile)
links its repository's `libz.a`. Its precise zlib version is not identified in the
published npm metadata; the upstream zlib notice is included conservatively.

API evidence: xmllint's published browser module contains the Emscripten `Module`
factory used by its Worker wrapper; the adapter supplies in-memory XML/schema
files, `--nonet --noout --schema`, a WASM binary and bounded imported memory.
The XSLT package's `dist/xslt-wasm.js` exposes `createXSLTTransformModule`,
`cwrap('transform', ...)`, `_malloc`, `_free`, and `wasmMemory`; its
[C entry point](https://github.com/mfreed7/xslt_polyfill/blob/main/src/transform.c)
accepts input/style byte pointers and lengths and returns an allocated result.
Both factories run in disposable workers with network access disabled. These
adapters are pinned to the exact package versions above; review the ABI and
rerun the browser tests before upgrading.

===== wordperfect-root-THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md =====
Source: wordperfect-root-THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md (packages/renderers/wordperfect/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md)
# Third-party notices

- `libwpd` 0.10.3 and `librevenge` 0.0.6 are compiled to WebAssembly under their MPL-2.0 license arm. The complete license is included in `vendor/libwpd-src/LICENSE.MPL-2.0.txt`.
- The callback bridge is derived from the MIT-licensed `xberg-libwpd` shim. Its license is included verbatim in `vendor/libwpd-src/LICENSE.xberg-shim-MIT.txt`.
- A header-only Boost 1.90 subset is present at build time under BSL-1.0. It is checksum-pinned and described in `vendor/libwpd-src/PROVENANCE.md`.
- The native runtime uses Emscripten 6.0.9 (official commit
  `4e4223852a0835923411059a3929907d7df1232e`) and zlib 1.3.2. Its actual system
  link inputs are libc, libc++, libc++abi, compiler-rt builtins, dlmalloc and
  zlib. Their complete upstream grants and notices are retained as
  `vendor/libwpd-src/LICENSE.toolchain-*`; see `NATIVE_PROVENANCE.json` in that
  directory for exact source and output identities. The covered parser and
  bridge sources remain unchanged.

Self-hosted asset copies include this notice, native provenance, and a
`licenses/` directory. Preserve them alongside the Worker, module and WASM.

The runtime distribution excludes source archives and build instructions. The
matching public source archives are available from the fixed Xberg commit
`db5ff1624cb0307ebca7cafb2af8fa6c6f93f2b4`:

- [libwpd 0.10.3 source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xberg-io/xberg/db5ff1624cb0307ebca7cafb2af8fa6c6f93f2b4/crates/xberg-libwpd/vendor/libwpd-0.10.3.tar.gz), SHA-256 `ca3575282acff8c952c12160433ad7e73e803ff3f070b8442c7ffa1f3a19f9ae`.
- [librevenge 0.0.6 source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xberg-io/xberg/db5ff1624cb0307ebca7cafb2af8fa6c6f93f2b4/crates/xberg-libwpd/vendor/librevenge-0.0.6.tar.gz), SHA-256 `686cc36be3196a0a808761cfd3951a46ff809cb0e028b0902c787261a1389d0f`.
- [Boost 1.90 header subset](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xberg-io/xberg/db5ff1624cb0307ebca7cafb2af8fa6c6f93f2b4/crates/xberg-libwpd/vendor/boost-subset.tar.gz), SHA-256 `802ee17c5e380efbcbb696468ee3c7090aa409db89c2063b4c9b8d3e3aff1e08`.

The WebAssembly runtime is lazy-loaded by the WordPerfect Worker. The bounded TypeScript signature/text fallback remains separate and is not presented as equivalent fidelity.

===== wordperfect-vendor_libwpd-src-PROVENANCE.md =====
Source: wordperfect-vendor_libwpd-src-PROVENANCE.md (packages/renderers/wordperfect/vendor/libwpd-src/PROVENANCE.md)
# libwpd WebAssembly provenance

The WordPerfect Worker builds the following sources under their documented license arms:

- `libwpd-0.10.3.tar.gz` — checksum-pinned, pruned source archive derived from upstream `libwpd` 0.10.3 by Xberg (public headers, implementation sources and license files retained), MPL-2.0 OR LGPL-2.1-or-later; this build selects MPL-2.0. SHA-256 `ca3575282acff8c952c12160433ad7e73e803ff3f070b8442c7ffa1f3a19f9ae`.
- `librevenge-0.0.6.tar.gz` — checksum-pinned, pruned source archive derived from upstream `librevenge` 0.0.6 by Xberg (public headers, implementation sources and license files retained), MPL-2.0 OR LGPL-2.1-or-later; this build selects MPL-2.0. SHA-256 `686cc36be3196a0a808761cfd3951a46ff809cb0e028b0902c787261a1389d0f`.
- `boost-subset.tar.gz` — the header-only Boost 1.90 dependency closure generated with `bcp`, BSL-1.0. SHA-256 `802ee17c5e380efbcbb696468ee3c7090aa409db89c2063b4c9b8d3e3aff1e08`.
- `shim.cpp` — the callback-to-structured-event bridge derived from `xberg-libwpd`, MIT. Its license is included as `LICENSE.xberg-shim-MIT.txt`.

The source archives are checksum-verified by `scripts/build-libwpd-wasm.mjs` before each build. The generated `dist/libwpd.mjs` and `dist/libwpd.wasm` are lazy-loaded only by the WordPerfect Worker. Current generated SHA-256 values are `ccd3267ce9cac2961bb6a500761753efa05c93563e7a5e46a31594cceb5e3096` (`libwpd.mjs`) and `bbfe0c7f712a357e3f9d11f9cf96d931e7cf4b9165d4379af78bf1bcb69333f0` (`libwpd.wasm`).

The normal native build requires Emscripten 6.0.9, whose official source commit
is `4e4223852a0835923411059a3929907d7df1232e`, and its checksum-pinned zlib 1.3.2
port. `NATIVE_PROVENANCE.json` identifies the actual linked system libraries and
their original full license/notice files. The libwpd, librevenge and bridge
sources above remain unchanged. Preserve the `LICENSE.toolchain-*` documents
when redistributing the native runtime and its self-hosted assets.

Sources:

- https://downloads.sourceforge.net/project/libwpd/libwpd/libwpd-0.10.3/libwpd-0.10.3.tar.gz
- https://downloads.sourceforge.net/project/libwpd/librevenge/librevenge-0.0.6/librevenge-0.0.6.tar.gz
- https://github.com/xberg-io/xberg/tree/main/crates/xberg-libwpd

# Rust/WASM third-party licenses

This document is the binary-distribution license inventory for the Rust crates
resolved by `rust/Cargo.lock` and used to build `chm_wasm_bg.wasm`.

- Cargo.lock SHA-256: `8a81680e7a32a1d88656a148834dc24eb6bf866bd1366d836abac1c95e6b86ea`
- Inventory command: `cargo metadata --locked --format-version 1`
- Audit date: 2026-09-01
- Registry source: the exact crate versions named below from crates.io.
- For `MIT OR Apache-2.0` packages this distribution elects Apache-2.0.
  The complete Apache-2.0 text is reproduced in section A.
- Build/procedural dependencies are included as well as runtime dependencies so
  the inventory is a conservative superset of code that can affect the WASM artifact.
- No crate in this lockfile has an upstream `NOTICE` file.

The “upstream attribution” column is copied from Cargo package metadata unless a
packaged license or copyright file supplies a more specific copyright notice.

===== ppt-runtime-NOTICE.md =====
Source: ppt-runtime-NOTICE.md (apps/viewer-demo/public/vendor/ppt/NOTICE.md)
# Source and distribution notice

Copyright 2026 Flyfish. The published TypeScript PPT runtime is distributed under Apache-2.0. The development source repository remains private. The public npm archive contains compiled JavaScript, declarations, this notice and the license; it does not contain TypeScript implementation files, source maps, private QA reports, documents or fonts. This grant does not apply to previous native/WASM package versions, which retain their original licenses.

The following foundation originated in the user's `flyfish-dev/msdoc-viewer` repository, main commit `a42f4a28cad75db19021ef70eaa8c10548e0eb26`, retrieved for this task:

- Binary reader and utility conventions used by `src/core/binary.ts`, `utils.ts`, `xml-text.ts`.
- Pure TypeScript DEFLATE code used by `src/core/inflate.ts`, with explicit output limits and exact-size/checksum validation added in this delivery.
- WMF/EMF-to-SVG conversion and vector font helpers used by `src/core/vector.ts` and `vector-font.ts`, with additional record, allocation and output bounds, bitmap transforms, alpha handling and SVG image-link compatibility in this delivery. The reused converter and its new extensions remain partial implementations of the metafile formats.
- Architecture and small geometry conventions from the project's container, worker, model, preset and shape-geometry modules. The new PPT container/persist/text/drawing logic was not copied from a legacy PowerPoint engine.

Exact origin paths, destination paths and local hashes are recorded in `docs/provenance.json`. The reuse is intentional and authorized by the user's instruction to base this work on msdoc-viewer; it is not presented as independently authored foundation code.

Microsoft Open Specifications are the normative PPT/CFB/OfficeArt/crypto format sources. TIFF and PICT use the original Aldus TIFF 6.0 and Apple Inside Macintosh QuickDraw specifications. SVG output follows the relevant W3C SVG specification; the Base64 encoder was independently authored from RFC 4648's alphabet, bit grouping and padding rules and checked against its standard test vectors. Links and field notes appear in `docs/spec-notes.md`, `docs/officeart.md`, `docs/renderer.md`, `docs/images.md` and `docs/encryption.md`. The specifications and their reference implementations are not redistributed as part of this source bundle.

Independent test documents from the Apache POI test-data collection were used as black-box inputs. No POI parser source files were fetched or used to implement this parser, and no third-party parser code was copied or translated. Their original document bytes are excluded from this delivery; provenance identifiers and validation outcomes are retained. Authorized private inputs include native binary `.ppt` and `.pot` files and a larger binary `.ppt` produced by LibreOffice from a PPTX solely for testing. This converted case is identified separately from native inputs; it does not add PPTX support to the product. Original and converted private documents, their page images and full requested-to-resolved font manifests remain outside the repository and package. `fixtures/showcase.ppt`, `fixtures/playback.ppt`, their PNG/PCM media, raster patterns and handcrafted encrypted fixtures were authored by the included independent fixture writers.

## External QA tools and distribution boundary

The following tools operate outside the production TypeScript implementation:

- **LibreOffice** is a black-box executable for test conversion and independent reference exports. Its implementation source was not read, copied or translated into this parser or renderer.
- **`@napi-rs/canvas`** supplies native Canvas measurements only to an explicitly selected external Node QA adapter. The adapter and native package are not bundled or required by the viewer.
- **Noto CJK, other system fallback fonts and Fontconfig** provide the QA environment's actual font files and family resolution. These fonts can differ from the document's requested fonts and PowerPoint's environment. No font binaries are shipped with the product.
- **Inkscape** exports SVG to PNG for limited visual inspection. Its consumer-specific rendering limitations, including the observed nested SVG clipping issue, are not browser or PowerPoint acceptance evidence.
- **Pillow** is an independent TIFF test encoder and pixel reference. It is not runtime code or a runtime dependency.

`package.json` declares no production, optional, peer or bundled dependencies. TypeScript, Playwright and the consumer build tools are development dependencies only. The public package allowlist contains compiled modules, declarations, README and license notices. It excludes development tools, source maps, TypeScript implementation files, QA adapters, native libraries, font binaries, private inputs, reference images and internal documentation. The private repository retains the engineering provenance and regression records.

This project's production runtime does not include or depend on the existing pptjs native/WASM engine, third-party PowerPoint parsers, proprietary Office binaries, external QA tools or font binaries. The cleanroom engineering claim is limited to independently implementing PPT-specific logic from documented format information, with the above reused foundation and black-box validation disclosed. It is not a legal certification or a separately audited two-team cleanroom process. Source provenance, successful parsing and agreement with an external QA renderer do not establish complete specification coverage or PowerPoint pixel equivalence; the implementation and evidence boundaries are tracked in `docs/spec-coverage.json` and `docs/spec-coverage.md`.

===== npm-isarray-README.md =====
Source: npm-isarray-README.md (node_modules/isarray/README.md)

# isarray

`Array#isArray` for older browsers.

[![build status](https://secure.travis-ci.org/juliangruber/isarray.svg)](http://travis-ci.org/juliangruber/isarray)
[![downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dm/isarray.svg)](https://www.npmjs.org/package/isarray)

[![browser support](https://ci.testling.com/juliangruber/isarray.png)
](https://ci.testling.com/juliangruber/isarray)

## Usage

```js
var isArray = require('isarray');

console.log(isArray([])); // => true
console.log(isArray({})); // => false
```

## Installation

With [npm](http://npmjs.org) do

```bash
$ npm install isarray
```

Then bundle for the browser with
[browserify](https://github.com/substack/browserify).

With [component](http://component.io) do

```bash
$ component install juliangruber/isarray
```
